scope: Standing heritage exteriors of the Parramatta Female Factory and adjacent former Roman Catholic Orphan School and Parramatta Girls Home, including the two original sandstone ranges, penitentiary dormitory, solitary-cell enclosure wall, the school’s main building and its covered way and southwest range.
stage: Parramatta standing precinct footprints and Qualla original prepared

mappedIdentity.name: Parramatta Female Factory and Institutions Precinct
mappedIdentity.surveyedSeparateIdentity: Female Factory and former Roman Catholic Orphan School, with C105 positioned using government plan AR.S60.1001.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The two 1821 ranges, the sandstone 1826 penitentiary and the 1839 enclosing wall survive. The original cell block is gone. The orphan school’s main sandstone and brick building, covered way, chapel and brick ranges remain south of the wall.

The two original outer ranges were altered after the factory era. The surviving C105 masonry ward was built in two joined sections for third-class women. The original central barracks were demolished in the 1880s.

The labelled north precinct ground plan distinguishes the two ranges from the reused clock building and records the approximate location and envelope of the penitentiary block. The existing C111 roof and elevation schedules record a tiled roof, dormers and chimneys.

N01 has a three- and four-storey sandstone Georgian center and brick, stone-dressed Victorian wings. It has a slate roof and a later verandah partially enclosing the central portico. N02 is a timber covered way linking the main building to the southwest range.
